Combined Hero-cum-Sati Stone.title: Combined Hero-cum-Sati Stone
Combined Hero-cum-Sati Stone.detailed_description: Bi-panelled hero-cum-sati stone commemorating a hero who died a heroic death and his faithful wife who followed him to the pyre (funeral fire). The lowermost panel represents the faithful wife standing with folded hands before her husband's pyre. Ready to self immolate; she is flanked be devotees. Musicians are depicted within a structural frame just below the sati; they are playing drum and gong. The upper panel illustrates the enthroned hero in heaven seated on a high throne and his wife on a lower throne to his left side. The heroic couple are shown as attended and worshipped by apsaras and devotees. The roof topping of the slab has a kalasha on its apex which is slightly damaged.

In the middle row one man standing holding sword and shield, other man standing in thribhanga. In third row worship of Agni by a man standing. Inscription in three lines. (Marati).
Combined memorial stone.detailed_description: Inscribed Viragal in three panels. The lowermost panel illustrates a sati (faithful wife) about to immolate herself in the funeral fire of her husband who died a heroic death. The middle panel depicts the hero about to start a combat with his enemy. The uppermost panel represents the hero seated on a throne in heaven; he is depicted as welcoming his wife who is standing on his proper right side to his heavenly abode.

Ganesha.detailed_description: Defaced, large, image of Ganesha carved out of a crude Basalt stone. The seated, two handed image has a large torso with broad shoulders giving a giant look to the figure. Face, hands and belly are damaged. The right hand is probably in abhayamudra (blessing) and in the left hand the deity is (probably) holding modhaka (sweet). Trunk and sacred thread around the body are visible. The figure is treated roughly without any embellishment or ornamentation.

All three panels are broken.The lowermost panel which usually illustrates the cause of hero's death is broken. The middle panel represents the hero being carried to heaven by a mob of apsaras. The uppermost panel depicts the hero seated in heaven, worsipping a shivalinga; a person, probably a dwarpalaka holding a sword and a shield is guarding him. This memorial stone can be assigned to 13th cent. A.D. (later phase of Goa Kadambas) because the heads of the figures increase disproportionately to the size of their bodies.

Her left leg is placed on the back of a demon Buffalo. The pedestal and prabhavali are decorated with flower motifs.
Mahisasura Mardini.detailed_description: Four handed heavy ornamented Mahisasura-Mardhini image in high relief carved out of a plaque of basalt bordered by torana decoration. The deity wears necklace, waist band, armlets and kirithmukuta with a kirtimuka on top. The goddess is depicted in her usual form of killing the Mahisha. Her upper right hand controls Mahisha with a javelin, lower right hand strikes a sword into Mahisha's head, and lower left hand pierces a dagger into Mahisha's mouth; the upper left hand holds a lotus. The goddess is depicted in her usual posture; her right leg rests on the ground and left on the back of Mahisha.

The godess is represented in her furious form the Mahisasuramardini, killing the demon Mahisha; her right foot is resting on the ground and left foot on the back of the Mahisha. She is holding ayuda in three hands and a lotus in the upper left hand; the upper right hand is striking a sword into the head of Mahisha and the lower left hand is piercing a dagger into the mouth of Mahisha. The goddess wears kiritha mukuta and prabhavali around her head.

Metalic Block with Portuguese Emblem.title: Metalic Block with Portuguese Emblem
Metalic Block with Portuguese Emblem.detailed_description: The metal block has a distinctive design, featuring a square face that prominently displays the Portuguese emblem. This is likely intended to be visually striking and easily recognizable. The back of the block is semi-circular in shape, which suggests it was designed for attachment to a machine used for printing purposes. The semi-circular shape would allow for secure fixing to the machine. Two small spindles or spears are located at each corner of the square face, possibly serving as centring aids during the printing process. These features indicate that the block was designed with functionality and precision in mind.

Model of Fort of Diu.title: Model of Fort of Diu
Model of Fort of Diu.detailed_description: Model of fort of Diu showing two different styles of fortification: (i) the usual style consisting of round bastions prevailant all over the world which was known in Europe as the old Italian style (bastions broken at places). (ii) Later, as a second belt of fortification, wall I was added in 'heco' i.e.Italian in style consisting of heart shaped bastions which contained mathematical gunfire storerooms with hidden openings in front of the rampart walls. This special fortification design was invented in Italy towards the middle of 16th century from where it had spread to all over Europe. With the advent of Portuguese, this style travelled to India. Statue in Bronze of Afonso de Albuquerqu.detailed_description: The statue is a representation of Alfonso de Albuquerque, the Governor of Portuguese India from 1510 A.D. It depicts him in a standing pose and features a notable characteristic - a long curly beard. The statue also shows Albuquerque wearing chain ornaments and holding a sword in his hand. Its dimensions are significant: it stands at a height of 3.10 meters and has a breadth of 1.20 meters.

Surya.title: Surya
Surya.brief_description: A sculpture in stone of Surya.
Surya.detailed_description: Richly embllished standing image of Suryadeva (sungod) flanked by attendants- danda and pingala. The two handed deity holds full blown lotuses in both the hands; the image is depicted with heavy ornamentation - kiritha mukutha, karnakundala, necklaces, chest ornamentation, katibanda (waist band). The deity wears boot till the knees- probably the influence of kushana art. The personification of Surya and his worship as a deity with other deities like Shiva, Vishnu, Shakti and Ganesha became popular in India from the Gupta period. Surya had been worshipped as a deity from ancient times by the Hindu populations of Goa region.

Torso of a deity.title: Torso of a deity
Torso of a deity.provenance: Old Talab near Bhagavati shrine of villages virnora, pernem tq. Goa.
Torso of a deity.brief_description: One relief of Ravalnath in half relief. It is broken in four pieces. The head is mutilated. A little evidence is left. Legs below the knee broken . It is in the very bad state of preservation. The image of Ravalnath was worshipped as a 'Bhkshatanamurthi' or 'Pari- varadevata' (family god) by the Hindu populations of Goa, particularly the cattle raising communities during ancient and medieval times.
Torso of a deity.detailed_description: The crude relief sculpture depicts four-handed Ravalnath, although it is damaged with the head and legs below the knee being broken. Additionally, the attributes associated with this image are lost. The image of Ravalnath was conceived as a form of Shiva by the Hindu populations of Goa through the ages.

Uma-Maheshwar.detailed_description: Ornamented, headless, relief of Uma-Maheshwar image (mutilated) seated in abida (folded legs with feet touching each other) posture. parvati is seated on the lap of her spouse. The couple is embracing each other. Both the deities are depicted with elaborate ornamentation. Heads and hands of the deities are broken and attributes are lost.

Uma-Maheshwar in round.title: Uma-Maheshwar (in round)
Uma-Maheshwar in round.brief_description: A highly ornamented sculpture of Uma-Maheshwar in alingana posture.
Uma-Maheshwar in round.detailed_description: A highly ornamented sculpture of Uma-Maheshwar in alingana posture wearing jatha mukutha with depiction of elaborate, ornamental prabhavali behind their heads. Right hand of Mahesh is in abhayamudra and the left arm is embracing Uma on her shoulder. Uma is depicted with four hands. One right arm is broken and the other is embracing Mahesh. In the left hand she is holding a lotus (only the stem is visible) and in the other hand she is holding a mirror. Both the deities are adorned with elaborate ornamentation.

Vetal.title: Vetal
Vetal.detailed_description: Mutilated, ornamented Vetala image. Lower portion is broken and missing Vetala wears a garland of skulls and a kirita mukutha with depiction of snake; ribs are visible on its chest; it has projecting eyes and elongated ears and wears a scorpion on its abdomen.

Vishnu.title: Vishnu
Vishnu.provenance: From inner sanctum of Mahadeva temple near Curdi village, Goa.
Vishnu.brief_description: Standing Vishnu figure mutilated not compete part of Acc no 05
Vishnu.detailed_description: Right portion of the broken frame of a Vishnu Vimana figure showing two standing attendents. One is holding a snake and the other one is in Kalihasta (empty hand). The main deity Vishnu was initially flanked by - two elephants and four attendants (two on each side)and one yati.

Vishnu Dashavathara on Prabhavli.title: Vishnu (Dashavathara on Prabhavli)
Vishnu Dashavathara on Prabhavli.brief_description: Image of Vishnu prabhavali carved with Dasavathara. Prabhavali broken but horse piece available. Front hands broken.
Vishnu Dashavathara on Prabhavli.detailed_description: Richly emblished slenderly carved image of Vishnu with details of Dashavtara. The four handed deity wears heavy ornamentation - kirita mukutha (crown) necklaces, armlets, ear-rings, katibandha (waist band), ornamental yajnopavita (scared thread) and anklets; the lower portion of the image is covered with the characteristic costume of vaishnative images with elaborate liner drapery falling from waist-line till the feet on either side. Three hands below the elbow are broken and attributes are lost. Vishnu is flank-ed by two adoring female figures and the prabhavali around his head represents his Dashavtara Matsya, kurma, Varaha, Vamana, Narasinvha, Rama, Parshurama, Krishna, Buddha, Kalki etc.

The warrior is depicted with minimum dress code of a kampina held by three stranded girdles around his waist.
